summary: GLM-5.3 (744B) holds 15-55% more KV tokens and decodes faster at TP8 and TP6; TP8 DCP=2 and TP6 DCP=3 now serve a 1M context without running out of memory
compatibility: glm53-csf-tp8 fixes the KV size at DCP > 1 and glm53-csf-tp6 at every DCP size (KV_CACHE_MEMORY_BYTES overrides it). GLM-5.3 presets turn on the DCP prefill gathers when DCP > 1 (DCP_CKV_GATHER=0 turns them off). Other models are unchanged.
details: glm53-csf-tp8 and glm53-csf-tp6 quantize the checkpoint's BF16 attention and shared experts to MXFP8 while loading (new option quantization-config), run the MTP layer's attention and shared experts in MXFP8 and its routed experts W4A16 NVFP4 on B12X, and draft with an NVFP4 copy of the vocabulary head.

TP8 on 8x RTX PRO 6000: DCP1 616,448 KV tokens (535,808 before), decode steps/s C1 / C2 / C4 89.8 / 144.0 / 213.5 (83 / 138 / 196 before); DCP2 1,186,944 tokens (the full 1,048,576-token context), 76.2 / 123.6 / 184.6, prefill 7,771 / 7,420 tok/s at 8K / 128K.

With DCP > 1, GLM-5.3 prefill gathers the full compressed KV cache and the indexer keys (vLLM #998); DCP6 and TP8 gather up to the full 1M context. A needle is found near the longest context at every size, up to 1.03M tokens at TP6 DCP6.

Presets can fix the KV cache per DCP size (kv_bytes_by_dcp). With DCP, context-sized indexer and exchange buffers grow outside vLLM's budget: at 92% of GPU memory a 1M-token prompt ran TP8 DCP2 out of memory. Every size now leaves at least 500 MiB free per GPU through a prompt at the longest context, 64 concurrent 8K prompts and four minutes of 1K-96K prompts.
TP8 DCP4 and DCP8 (27 GiB per GPU, 4.24M tokens at DCP8) prefill only about 800 tokens/s while new prompts overlap running requests.
